pr_title: Fix reloading current scene forgetting path
pr_body:
Scene was stopped before running which cleared the last run scene, forcing it to run the currently edited scene instead

* Fixes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/87163

pr_comments:
The Play Current Scene button changes icon and tooltip when the project is running.
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/2223172/a6dce39f-d56f-4a9d-836e-2b901f36d07a)
The current behavior is intended (see #58665)

So the current behavior is against the tooltip? Also why does it save the current scene?

The expected behavior:
* Reloads the scene that was played last, not the open tab

That was the wording in that PR, and seems to have been the behavior before the relocation of the run bar into its own file, from #76026

So to confirm, the intended behavior is to run the scene open in the editor tab, not the scene that is running as the button is played? If that's the case the tooltip should be changed as it's misleading

Ok I misunderstood 🙃
Sounds like it's indeed a bug and it should reload the running scene. Though this behavior was discussed after my change and it possibly has changed since then.
It seems to be an oversight, as the line saves the variable, even though it would always be empty at that point

I think there's been confusion around what should be the behavior, and if the "expected" behavior is not currently working, I'm worried it might have become the de facto expectation from users.

When this was changed (apparently it was working initially), users complained about the change of behavior compared to Godot 3:
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75998
- https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6550

So I'm worried that this bugfix might be unpopular.

Personally I find the behavior of running the previously ran scene if it's still running... confusing, as its description sounds. But it depends on each user's workflow. Usually if I have a scene still running, and I'm using the editor viewing another scene, it's typically that I don't really care anymore about the currently open instance, and next time I press F6 I want to run the scene I'm inspecting. I can see how others might have a different workflow.

Overall, I feel this bugfix might need to go together with a solution for https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6550, and remove this IMO confusing hybridation of the F6 button.
We could either move the reload behavior to another button (e.g. Run Project) or add a new button for reloading scenes.

At least the tooltip would need changing, the description is "Reload the played scene" which cannot be interpreted in any other way IMO, how is loading a new scene "reloading"?

This is a regression from relocating the run bar, it worked before, and the code in place is for this behavior, otherwise that code makes no sense

So this restores intended behavior, and fixes an oversight in previous PRs, at least if the current behavior is kept the tooltip must be updated

> at least if the current behavior is kept the tooltip must be updated

And the icon too, because the button changes into reload.

> So this restores intended behavior, and fixes an oversight in previous PRs, at least if the current behavior is kept the tooltip must be updated

My point is, the intended behavior was opposed by some users shortly after it was implemented, and then eventually an unintended regression "fixed" the change to restore the 3.x behavior by error.

So this to me is a strong indication that we need to properly assess what users want, and not what was approve back in 2022 and led to this tooltip saying this :)

Well I'd say to fix this now and discuss it, or change the tooltip and icon now, and discuss it, but currently it causes confusion (evidently from the report)

We'd also have to change the behaviour of the `Run Custom` for parity as it also reloads, lack of parity there would be confusing as well

The current state is the most confusing, and this fix is the least complex (and arguably least disruptive, you can easily achieve this by stopping the scene, but the opposite isn't true)

Further I'd argue that reverting that improvement by effectively accepting this bug (which several code changes and design changes) worsens workflow, possible senario:
* Using a main scene, like a testing ground scene, to test various components, such as a player, an enemy, etc.
* Run the main scene, then do some testing, go to the player scene, do some editing, reload running scene

If you now want the 3.x behavior you just press the "stop" button, and then the "run current scene" button, trivial

However if we revert that improvement now you have to move back and forth between scenes in the editor to re-run the scene you're using as a base, this is *much* more disruptive than having to press two buttons instead of one IMO

I'd say this can be discussed further, but I don't think leaving a regression in place even with fixes to fix the confusing things, is a good workflow, and at least this needs to be fixed in one way or another, because the current state is confusing

If we worry about breaking expectations of people who are currently used to the status quo, let's avoid cherry-picking this fix and introduce it in 4.3. We can also make it an option, if the opinions are so evenly split we can't decide on the most optimal solution.
I agree on the cherry pick, let's discuss it for the backwards cases and optionality etc.

issue_context.title: "Reload the played scene" (F6) is launching the currently focused tab, not reloading the previously selected scene
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.2.1 Stable
Not Reproducible in 4.0.4

### System information

Godot v4.2.1.stable - Windows 10

### Issue description

I recently upgraded from 4.0.4 to 4.2.1 and suddenly the reload button is launching the currently focused scene tab instead of the scene previously selected to run.

This behavior is different than before when it would reload the previously selected scene.

It is important for this button to work correctly so I can deliberately test a (not main) scene while using the editor tabs to update and fix other scenes that are part of it.
For example, the main scene of my project is a "Menu" scene but I am developing an "Arena" scene with a "Character" and a new "Obstacle".
I select the Arena and press the "Run Current Scene (F6)" button so I can test the interaction between the Character and the Obstacle
I then use the editor tabs to inspect and make changes to the child scenes.
Previously I would then press the "Reload the Played Scene" button to re-launch the Arena and test my updates, but instead it will launch the currently focused tab, be it the Character or Obstacle, which is not helpful for testing interaction.

Is there a setting somewhere that I've overlooked? Thanks

### Steps to reproduce

Pick a scene, launch it.
Switch a tab.
Try to relaunch the scene you picked.
Notice that it launches the currently focused tab instead.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

-
comments: I've identified the cause of this bug, will write a fix

I pulled your fix and applied it to the 4.2.1-stable branch, built it, and it works like a charm. Thank you so much for knowing right where to look! Looking forward to seeing your fix merged for future releases.
This hasn't been fixed yet so please leave it open until merge
